Hi Friend,

I am going to address each number you put in there.

1) Kick out illegals, supply of workers diminishes forcing higher wages along with cutting national budget. A: The wages would only be higher for farming, fast food, and hotels. And by higher I mean they would be at minimum wage since a lot of people who use illegals pay below the minimum since there is risk in using them. These higher wages would drive higher prices in these industries therefore kicking off higher inflation. This higher inflation might not be a bad thing since the Fed wants a target of around 2% which they are finding hard to hit. Prices would rise on food, which is a large portion of the basket of goods used to determine inflation. So long as the inflation does not get out of control by removing roughly 10% of the working population in these industries, this would not be bad. The down side would be that a lot of people don't want these jobs so there might be shortages in labor and also some companies might close up shop since the increased labor costs might make their businesses not viable. I would predict that this might have a neutral effect, but could swing positive or negative.

2) Cut off free trade deals and raise tariffs forcing companies to move back here A: I don't see how this would work? We are in these trade deals, which are approved by congress, I don't believe that a president can just cancel a trade deal without an act of congress. Not to mention that these deals may have penalties for cancellation. I could be wrong about this. Also you would need to look into US laws but I don't believe a US company that produces products outside of the US would be forced to pay a tariff once it brings the product back into the US, once again I could be wrong. Trump is first and foremost a businessman, I can not believe that he would risk the wrath that could be unleashed on his businesses. Another point to consider would be that adding tariffs to imported goods would again create inflation, and a lot of it.
